items.prompt: A support team wants to compare a new prompt with the live prompt for account-routed traffic while tracking resolution, escalation, latency, cost, and safety. Which experiment design is strongest?
constraints: Accounts can receive stable treatment assignment.
Primary and guardrail metrics and a safety stop rule can be declared before launch.
Traffic is sufficient for the planned comparison.

options.text: Offer the new prompt to volunteers and compare their results with everyone else.
Randomize accounts, predeclare metrics, meet the sample, and review slices and transcripts.
Deploy the new prompt to everyone and compare this week’s averages with last week’s.
Ask support agents which prompt sounds better and use their preference as the rollout decision.

feedback.Reason: Stable account randomization limits crossover and confounding, while predeclared metrics, safety stopping, and slice review make the live comparison interpretable.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic recommends a small pilot, A/B infrastructure, human feedback, and updating offline evaluations from production data; assignment and stopping rules are scenario controls.
Details.scenarioApplication: Assign accounts once, measure resolution and guardrails by cohort, review representative transcripts, and stop for a predefined safety breach.
Details.errorCorrection: Volunteer, time-based, and preference comparisons confound treatment with user mix, traffic changes, or reviewer opinion.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: For a deterministic offline formatter with no user impact or side effects, a live randomized cohort would add little evidence.
Details.transfer: Use controlled exposure, predeclared outcomes, and qualitative review when testing a change on real users.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: Volunteers differ systematically from the target account population.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: Week-to-week traffic changes confound prompt effect with time and mix.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: Agent preference is not evidence of user outcomes or safety behavior.

items.prompt: Prompt B lifts correct claim resolution from 82% to 86% but raises p95 latency 40%, cost 25%, and safety escalations in a high-risk category. Account assignment and category slices are recorded. What should the team do?
constraints: The high-risk category has a stricter safety tolerance.
The experiment retains cohort and transcript evidence.
Latency, cost, and safety are guardrails rather than optional diagnostics.

options.text: Ship B because the overall resolution lift is positive and inspect the high-risk category later.
Average quality, latency, cost, and safety into one score and ship if it improves.
Review affected slices and keep safety, latency, and cost as guardrails before rollout.
Rollback both prompts and restart without using the recorded category evidence.

feedback.Reason: The headline lift cannot override a high-risk safety regression or violated operating limits; the stored cohort evidence should guide the constrained iteration.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic says A/B tests measure real user outcomes but need transcript review to explain changes, and evaluation layers are complementary.
Details.scenarioApplication: Review high-risk transcripts, quantify each guardrail by slice, and modify or limit B until it meets the declared boundaries.
Details.errorCorrection: Averages erase severity, and discarding the recorded evidence prevents diagnosis; resolution alone is not the release contract.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If B improved quality with no guardrail regression and all categories shared the same risk tolerance, broad rollout could follow the plan.
Details.transfer: Treat safety and operating commitments as gates around an experimental quality lift, then use slices and transcripts to decide the next change.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: A global lift cannot veto a safety regression in the category with stricter tolerance.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: A composite score can hide a hard guardrail breach.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: Restarting discards the cohort and transcript evidence needed to identify the trade-off.

items.prompt: A coding-agent model upgrade beats a small offline suite but can edit files and run commands in shared development environments. Select TWO rollout controls.
constraints: Sandboxed evaluation and a controlled canary are available.
Assignment and rollback criteria can be recorded.
Quality, safety, latency, and cost can be monitored by cohort.

options.text: Run the upgrade in a sandbox first and then expose a small reversible canary cohort with quality, safety, latency, and cost monitoring.
Roll out to every shared environment because the offline score is higher.
Let the model approve its own first deployment after it explains why the change is safe.
Define rollback criteria and preserve a control cohort while the canary runs.
Disable command execution during the canary, even though command behavior is part of the production contract.

feedback.Reason: Sandbox evidence and a small reversible cohort answer different questions; a control and explicit rollback limit the blast radius of tool side effects.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic recommends a small pilot, thorough evaluation, gradual scaling, A/B testing, and human oversight; the environment and rollback constraints are scenario controls.
Details.scenarioApplication: Test the model in isolation, assign a canary and control, watch guardrails, and revert when a declared criterion is breached.
Details.errorCorrection: Universal rollout removes comparison, self-approval is not independent evidence, and disabling tools changes the contract being tested.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the model had no tools or side effects and the offline suite covered a deterministic contract, a canary would add less safety evidence.
Details.transfer: Stage changes with isolated evidence, controlled exposure, an independent control, and a reversible rollback boundary.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: Universal exposure removes the control and expands side-effect risk before live behavior is known.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: A model’s explanation is not an independent deployment check.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.e: Removing command behavior tests a different system from the one that will be deployed.

omittedCorrectElementExplanationsByOptio.a: Sandbox evidence limits initial blast radius and the canary observes live behavior.
omittedCorrectElementExplanationsByOptio.d: A control and rollback rule preserve a reversible comparison while the canary is evaluated.

items.prompt: A document assistant produces three live failure patterns missing from its original offline suite. Engineers propose fixing tickets individually and leaving the suite unchanged. What should the team do?
constraints: Reports contain reproducible or reviewable inputs.
Cases can be triaged by impact and run in CI.
The curated suite still contains useful stable coverage.

options.text: Freeze the historical suite so its score remains comparable across releases.
Triage live failures, add representative regression cases and graders, rerun, and check prior behavior for regressions.
Replace the entire suite with the newest production reports, including duplicates and unreviewed cases, so the next release reflects only live failures.
Fix each ticket in production and let future user feedback decide whether the suite needs changes.

feedback.Reason: Production failures should become reviewed, repeatable regression evidence while the curated core remains intact and regression-tested.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic recommends a living evaluation suite combined with production monitoring and feedback as systems evolve.
Details.scenarioApplication: Reproduce and prioritize each pattern, add a representative case and grader to CI, verify the fix, and check prior cases for regressions.
Details.errorCorrection: Freezing preserves blind spots, wholesale replacement imports noise, and ticket-only fixes make future recurrence invisible.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If a report were an unverified anecdote with no reproducible input, investigate it before adding it as an evaluation case.
Details.transfer: Use production evidence to evolve a reviewed regression suite without discarding stable coverage.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: Freezing keeps the exact blind spots that production just exposed.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: Wholesale replacement loses stable coverage and can import duplicates or noise.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: A ticket fix without a regression case allows the same failure to return unnoticed.

items.prompt: An A/B test reports a 2% resolution lift after one day, but its predeclared sample target is not met, the confidence range overlaps, and guardrail data is sparse across account types. What decision is justified?
constraints: Account assignment is stable.
The owner can extend the run under the analysis plan.
The sample target, confidence rule, and stopping boundary were predeclared.

options.text: Ship the new variant because the early point estimate is positive.
Stop the experiment and declare no difference because the confidence range overlaps.
Continue under the sample plan or stop for a defined safety breach; inspect slices.
Change the stopping rule now so the positive estimate can be used for rollout.

feedback.Reason: An underpowered and uneven sample does not meet the declared evidence rule; continue under the plan or stop for a specified safety breach.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic notes that A/B tests measure real outcomes but are slower and need transcript review; the sample and stopping rules are scenario controls.
Details.scenarioApplication: Preserve assignment and analysis, collect the planned sample, monitor guardrails by account type, and review transcripts before declaring a winner.
Details.errorCorrection: A point estimate, a premature no-difference conclusion, or changing the stopping rule after seeing data turns noise into policy.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A completed planned sample with stable guardrails and a prespecified stopping rule could support rollout from the observed effect.
Details.transfer: Respect the evidence and stopping rule declared before an experiment, especially when safety coverage is incomplete.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: A positive early estimate may be noise in an incomplete sample.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: Overlapping confidence does not itself define the required stopping decision.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: Changing the rule after observing the result invalidates the planned evidence boundary.

items.prompt: Variant B reports a 4-point resolution lift. Account-level assignment was intended, but a routing bug sent 12% of users both variants; B also received twice as many easy premium accounts after a segment filter changed. Logs preserve crossover and composition. What should happen?
constraints: Exposure, account segment, session, and outcome logs are available.
The original plan requires clean account assignment and comparable segment mix.
The causal effect is needed before changing exposure.

options.text: Post-hoc weight the aggregate results by segment and ship B if the adjusted estimate remains positive across the contaminated sessions.
Discard the logs and use the unadjusted lift because the sample is large.
Ship only to premium accounts, where B has the largest observed lift.
Audit crossover and segments, restore account assignment, and rerun before changing exposure.

feedback.Reason: Crossover and changed composition contaminate treatment exposure and the counterfactual, so the apparent lift is not a valid causal comparison.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic describes A/B testing as controlling for confounds and requiring sufficient traffic and transcript review; crossover and segment balance are scenario controls.
Details.scenarioApplication: Use logs to quantify contamination, correct the routing and segment filter, preserve a clean cohort, and rerun before changing exposure.
Details.errorCorrection: Weighting cannot recover users who saw both variants or repair a changed exposure mechanism; an unadjusted or premium-only rollout compounds the confound.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If crossover were absent, segment mix matched the plan, and the sample met the analysis rule, the observed lift could proceed to the predeclared decision.
Details.transfer: Audit treatment exposure and population composition before interpreting a live comparison as causal.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: Weighting cannot restore the missing counterfactual for users exposed to both variants.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: A large contaminated sample remains causally invalid.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: Selecting the segment that received more favorable exposure turns the composition confound into a rollout rule.

items.prompt: An A/B test has a predeclared interim analysis at 1,000 eligible accounts, a stopping rule for a large reliable lift, and a safety guardrail. At the interim point, the sample target for the full study is not complete, but the predeclared lift and guardrails meet the documented decision boundary. What should the experiment owner do at this interim point?
constraints: The registered interim time, sample size, primary metric, uncertainty rule, guardrails, assignment log, and analysis output are immutable and available before the result is reviewed.

options.text: Complete the full sample target before applying the interim rule, so the study is not stopped on partial data.
Apply the registered interim rule, stop or advance as specified, preserve the analysis and guardrail evidence, and label the result as interim.
Declare a winner from the dashboard without applying the registered interim rule or preserving its analysis record.
Reset the experiment and collect a new sample because any decision before the final target is necessarily invalid.

feedback.Reason: Apply the registered interim rule, stop or advance exposure as it specifies, preserve the analysis and guardrail evidence, and report the decision as an interim-boundary outcome rather than an unplanned peek. The decisive constraint is A prespecified interim rule with sufficient evidence permits the declared decision; the absence of the final sample target alone does not require continuing when the rule authorizes stopping.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic recommends a small pilot, infrastructure for A/B testing, human feedback, and ongoing updates to offline evaluations from production data. The case-specific population, thresholds, roles, and authority limits are supplied by this scenario rather than by the provider documentation.
Details.scenarioApplication: Apply the registered interim rule, stop or advance exposure as it specifies, preserve the analysis and guardrail evidence, and report the decision as an interim-boundary outcome rather than an unplanned peek.
Details.errorCorrection: The first ignores an authorized stopping boundary; the second ignores the registered analysis and creates the unplanned-peeking problem covered by the rejected path. The competing action therefore leaves the stated decision boundary unresolved.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the interim rule were absent, the sample/uncertainty boundary unmet, or a safety guardrail breached, the experiment would continue or stop for the breach rather than declare this interim result.
Details.transfer: Use a prespecified stopping rule as the decision boundary and label the evidence according to the stage at which it was collected.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: The final sample target is not a prerequisite when the registered interim rule is met; waiting changes the declared decision point instead of applying it.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: A dashboard result without the registered rule recreates the unplanned-peeking problem.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: Resetting discards a valid prespecified boundary instead of applying the documented stopping decision.

items.prompt: A/B assignment is account-level, but support agents use one shared response playbook that contains Variant B's new instruction for both cohorts. Customer outcomes improve in both arms while account assignment logs remain balanced. Select TWO: Which actions repair the contaminated A/B comparison?
constraints: The playbook revision history, account assignment, agent exposure logs, and outcome transcripts are available; users in each arm can interact with the same support staff.

Exposure logs show that the same staff continue using the learned Variant B instruction across account assignments after the shared document is changed; changing the document alone does not remove staff-carried exposure.

options.text: Keep account-level assignment and credit Variant B because both cohorts received the same support volume.
Freeze and audit the shared playbook; quarantine and label contaminated observations, remove or version the cross-arm instruction, and record exposure evidence before the rerun.
Treat both cohorts as exposed to B and compare their aggregate outcomes without changing the assignment design.
Exclude support interactions from the analysis and infer the treatment effect from the balanced account logs alone.
Rerun a controlled comparison with arm-specific cluster or agent assignment because the same staff carry learned Variant B behavior across accounts, or fit an explicit residual-interference model.

feedback.Reason: Freeze and audit the shared playbook, quarantine and label contaminated observations, remove or version the cross-arm instruction, then rerun a controlled comparison with arm-specific cluster or agent assignment or an explicit residual-interference model. The same support staff carry learned Variant B behavior across accounts, so no single control restores a valid comparison by itself.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic says A/B tests measure real user outcomes but need transcript review to explain metric changes; multiple evaluation layers are complementary. The case-specific population, thresholds, roles, and authority limits are supplied by this scenario rather than by the provider documentation.
Details.scenarioApplication: Freeze and audit the shared playbook, quarantine and label contaminated observations, remove or version the cross-arm instruction, then rerun a controlled comparison with arm-specific cluster or agent assignment or an explicit residual-interference model.
Details.errorCorrection: The shared playbook makes both cohorts partially treated, so the observed lift cannot be attributed to B and could conceal harm in the intended control. The competing action therefore leaves the stated decision boundary unresolved.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If playbooks and agent exposure were isolated by arm, account-level randomization could support the existing A/B decision with the planned transcript review.
Details.transfer: Check the exposure path, not just assignment, whenever an operational artifact can cross experimental arms.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: The shared playbook partially treats both arms, so balanced assignment cannot identify B’s effect.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: Relabeling both arms does not recover a control group or explain the spillover.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: Removing the contaminated observations discards the exposure evidence and can hide harm in the intended control.

omittedCorrectElementExplanationsByOptio.b: Required control: Freeze and audit the shared playbook; quarantine and label contaminated observations, remove or version the cross-arm instruction, and record exposure evidence before the rerun.
omittedCorrectElementExplanationsByOptio.e: Required control: Rerun a controlled comparison with arm-specific cluster or agent assignment because the same staff carry learned Variant B behavior across accounts, or fit an explicit residual-interference model.
